Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Marketing Strategy & Operations team is responsible for driving organizational effectiveness and leading transformational programs across Marketing, Self-serve, Startup and Sales Development. We create the processes and conditions that enable high performance across teams and help Stripe scale with focus and discipline.

We partner closely with the CMO, Marketing and Sales Development leadership team to define strategy, lead operational planning, and steward execution across global programs. This role partners directly with the head of Global Demand, Campaigns, and Field Marketing. 

Our work spans cross-functional efforts that are critical to Stripe’s growth. From delivering strategic insights and frameworks to leading complex initiatives, we focus on what moves the needle most for the business. We care about results, not activity, and we have fun doing it. If you like hard problems, are analytical, and are an amazing teammate, we want to hear from you.

What you’ll do

Responsibilities

  • Drive our annual strategic plan and operating plan, working in partnership with the Global Demand, Campaigns, and Field Marketing leadership team to define our must-wins, build plans to win, and allocate our resources to deliver on the plan.
  • Define and manage our most critical OKRs that instill transparent, data-driven accountability for delivering our strategy to Stripe leadership.
  • Run the core rhythms of the business and reporting to focus attention, inspection, and strategic steers in the right places at the right time.
  • Drive critical leadership and team-wide communication forums (e.g. leadership onsites, all hands) to effectively cascade strategy and comms 
  • Leverage an AI-first approach to aggressively automate marketing reporting.
  • Bring clarity to ambiguity; navigate complexity, distill insight from noise, resolve issues quickly, and empower teams to make smart, confident decisions.
  • Work directly with senior leaders across the company and with cross-functional partners to accelerate progress, solve hard scaling initiatives, and incubate new programs.
  • Own and improve the campaign operations process end-to-end across digital campaigns and events - from planning and briefing through asset production, regional activation, and performance measurement - with a focus on efficiency and collaboration. 
  • Build tooling and automation to integrate marketing workflows and automate global calendars of marketing activity and impact
  • Define how we should effectively measure the success of our marketing efforts and align with Data, MarTech, and Eng teams to build the infrastructure to support our reporting goals
  • Use data to tell a compelling story and drive alignment on where we’re winning and where we need to focus.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 10 years of experience in consulting, strategy and operations, business operations, product strategy, product management, or similar roles with exposure to both business and technical skills
  • Proven people management experience leading a team in strategy and operations, marketing operations, or a similar function, with a track record of hiring, developing, and retaining high-performing talent
  • Background in B2B marketing, and core capabilities of Campaign and Field Marketing (e.g. digital campaigns, events)
  • Experience working in highly cross-functional settings, and in a role that spans strategy, analysis, and operations in a fast-paced environment
  • Critical and first-principles thinking, with the ability to zoom out to the most important questions 
  • Passion for digging deep into data to diagnose business issues and solve problems
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to speak to leaders across teams including product, engineering, analytics, sales, and partnerships
  • An ability to execute with minimal guidance and with a high degree of ambiguity

Preferred qualifications

  • Prior experience in payments, finance, fintech, or high-growth technology companies
  • Prior experience working directly with C-level executives and their direct reports
  • Experience navigating large data sets and/or SQL

descriptions.job-1ojl2x2:
US Filings Lead

Location: New York, NY (in office strongly preferred)

Type: Full-Time

About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world’s leading prediction markets platform and a CFTC-regulated designated contract market. We let people trade on real-world events, from political elections to sports outcomes to macroeconomic data releases, turning any question about the future into a tradeable contract. We’re building a new kind of information layer: fast, precise, and financially incentivized. Our markets have become a primary source of real-time probabilistic truth for millions of users. Now we’re looking for domain experts who can own what matters and ensure Polymarket is always first to cover it.

The Role

We’re hiring a US Filings Lead to work at the intersection of markets, compliance, and legal at Polymarket US. You’ll own the CFTC 40.2 self-certification and 40.6 rule amendment pipeline end to end, and work with the Markets team to structure new markets so they are both tradeable and certifiable.

This role requires understanding how markets work, not just how to file them: contract design, market structure, and the economic impact of fees and incentives, alongside the regulatory requirements. You’ll report to Compliance and work day to day with the Markets team in New York.

What You’ll Do

  • Work with the Markets team on new markets from the start: contract terms, settlement sources, and resolution criteria
  • Work with our compliance, fraud, surveillance, and market operations teams to design the infrastructure to build and surveil event contracts, futures, and perpetuals.
  • Draft and own 40.2 and 40.6 filing packages that hold up to CFTC review under the CEA and DCM Core Principles
  • Own filings for fees and incentive programs and understand how each affects liquidity and trading
  • Run the compliance-review gate
  • SLead high-stakes regulatory strategy and represent Polymarket US in complex negotiations with CFTC Division of Market Oversight (DMO) and Division of Clearing and Risk (DCR) staff, defending novel contract structures and preempting formal stays or disapprovals (e.g., Part 40.11 reviews)
  • Track listings and filings across the industry and flag what matters for us and why
  • Keep templates and the filing catalog current, and use AI and automation to speed up drafting, review, and the filing pipeline

-Architect the regulatory pathways for first-of-their-kind products—including event contracts, crypto derivatives, and perpetuals—translating ambiguous or evolving CEA interpretations into scalable, defensible market frameworks.

-Partner directly with Executive Leadership, Product, and Legal to evaluate commercial trade-offs, advise on regulatory risk appetite for high-profile markets, and inform long-term exchange roadmap decisions.

What You Bring

  • 7-12+ years at a DCM, SEF, DCO, FCM, or derivatives firm, or in a legal or regulatory practice serving them
  • Hands-on experience with CFTC certifications, rule filings, or exchange rulebooks
  • Strong grasp of market structure
  • Working knowledge of the CEA, CFTC Part 40, and the DCM Core Principles
  • Clear, precise writing for regulators and internal teams
  • Ability to balance quality and rigor with speed
  • Comfortable using AI tools in day-to-day work
  • Smart, reliable, low-ego, high-precision

Nice-to-Haves

  • JD, or a background in trading or market structure
  • Experience with event contracts or prediction markets
  • Direct experience working with CFTC staff
  • Experience automating document workflows (AI tools, SQL, scripting)

Submit the following alongside your resume:

  • Why US Filings Lead at Polymarket US?
  • A writing sample or paragraph on one of Polymarket US’s public filings and how you would draft it differently.

Job Description Summary

  • Mission: get new markets listed quickly, with filings that are correct, on time, and survive CFTC scrutiny
  • What you own: the 40.2/40.6 filing pipeline end to end; the regulatory side of market, fee, and incentive design; templates and the compliance-review gate
  • Reports to: Compliance; works day to day with the Markets team
  • Location: New York, in office
  • Success at 6–12 months: zero filing defects reaching the CFTC; faster turnaround; brought in at the design stage, not the filing stage; templates fully current

Who are we?

FalconX is a pioneering team of operators, investors, and builders committed to revolutionizing institutional access to the crypto markets. Operating at the intersection of traditional finance and  cutting-edge technology, FalconX addresses the industry's foremost challenges: Navigating the digital asset market can be complex and fragmented, with limited products and services that support trading strategies, structures, and liquidity found in conventional financial markets. As a comprehensive solution for all digital asset strategies from start to scale, FalconX operates as the connective tissue empowering clients with seamless navigation through the ever- evolving cryptocurrency landscape.

About the Role

We're looking for a hands-on Chartered Accountant with strong derivatives experience to run day-to-day accounting, product control, and financial reporting for our U.S. NFA/CFTC-regulated swap dealer and our international subsidiaries.

You'll work across both Product Control and Legal Entity Control. Your work will include daily derivative MTM and P&L, balance sheet close, and statutory reporting. You'll work closely with the Finance Manager, Front-Office Trading Desks, and Trade Operations, and help automate our processes in NetSuite.

What You'll Do

  1. Entity Accounting & Financial Close
  • Run monthly, quarterly, and annual close tasks under US GAAP and IFRS for the U.S. swap dealer entity and operating subsidiaries. This covers journal entries, accruals, intercompany eliminations, and balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Prepare balance sheet schedules and first drafts of statutory financial statements and footnote disclosures for the Manager to review. Disclosures include gross/net offsetting (ASC 210-20 / IFRS 7), fair value levels (ASC 820 / IFRS 13), and credit risk.
  • Monitor and settle intercompany balances, and support transfer pricing calculations, including intercompany crypto and derivative positions.
  1. Product Control & Derivatives Accounting
  • Run daily mark-to-market (MTM) and P&L for OTC and exchange-traded derivatives. Products include BTC/ETH options, systematic OTC trades, funded collars, total return swaps, interest rate swaps (IRS), and FX forwards.
  • Produce daily P&L attribution, explain P&L movements to Trading Desks, and investigate breaks with Trade Operations.
  • Support fair value leveling (Level 1–3), Expected Credit Loss (ECL) calculations, and margin and collateral reconciliations.
  • Research and draft accounting assessments (ASC 815 / IFRS 9) for new products such as digital asset lending, borrowing, staking, and principal market-making.
  1. Audit, Controls & Regulatory Support
  • Act as a day-to-day contact for Big 4 external auditors. Prepare PBC (provided-by-client) schedules, answer audit queries, and build historical workpapers.
  • Carry out legacy balance sheet cleanups and help draft technical GAAP position memos.
  • Run and document key controls under SOX 404 / ICFR, and keep Risk Control Matrices (RCMs) and SOPs up to date.
  • Provide financial data for regulatory and capital reporting under NFA, CFTC, and SEC rules and other global regimes, working with Compliance.
  1. Process Improvement & Team Support
  • Find manual spreadsheet workflows that can be automated, and help move them into NetSuite reporting.
  • Mentor and review the work of 1–2 junior associates or analysts.

What You Bring

Must-Have

  • Qualified Chartered Accountant (ICAI).
  • 5-8 years of experience in Product Control or Legal Entity Control at a Tier-1 investment bank (e.g., Goldman Sachs, Barclays, StanChart, BofA, Morgan Stanley), or in Big 4 Capital Markets / Financial Services audit or advisory.
  • Hands-on derivatives experience: daily MTM, P&L attribution, fair value measurement, and margin and collateral for OTC and/or exchange-traded derivatives.
  • Experience preparing balance sheet reconciliations, close schedules, and statutory disclosure schedules.
  • Strong working knowledge of US GAAP and IFRS, especially:
    • Derivatives: ASC 815 / IFRS 9
    • Fair value: ASC 820 / IFRS 13
    • Offsetting and disclosures: ASC 210 / IFRS 7
  • Advanced MS Excel skills and hands-on ERP experience (NetSuite preferred, or Oracle or SAP).
  • Based in Bengaluru, or willing to relocate, for a 3-day in-office hybrid schedule.

Good-to-Have

  • CPA, ACCA, or CFA (any level).
  • Exposure to crypto or digital asset accounting (ASC 350-60, IAS 38 / IAS 2) or crypto derivatives (perpetuals, funding rates).
  • Experience with SOX/ICFR controls 
  • Familiarity with crypto accounting tools (e.g., Bitwave, SoftLedger, Ledgible) or blockchain explorers.

How You Work

  • Detail-oriented and reliable, with strong analysis and problem-solving skills.
  • Clear communicator who can explain P&L and accounting positions to Traders, Operations, and auditors.
  • Keen to grow into a Manager role and to learn about digital assets and derivatives.

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken’s Core Infrastructure Engineering team builds and operates the shared data systems behind critical production services. Our estate spans on-premises and cloud infrastructure, with MariaDB at its centre and Kafka, Redis and Elasticsearch across the wider platform.

We’re hiring a Principal Database Engineer to bring long-term experience and technical judgment to this estate. You’ll assess it, set the goals and direction, and work hands-on with the team to deliver measurable improvements. This is an individual contributor role with influence across teams and several quarters of work.

 

The opportunity

  • Review the estate against business needs and production evidence. Judge reliability, scale, cost and operational complexity, identifying what should be preserved and where investment or simplification would make a difference.

  • Define the target architecture and measurable goals. Agree a prioritised roadmap with engineering leads and dependent teams, explaining the trade-offs and sequencing work around delivery risks.

The 4 biggest blockchain strengths are also its weakness

  • Permissionless nature leads to fragmentation of meaning

  • Decentralization leads to too many standards

  • Immutability leads to exponential data + query infrastructure complexity

  • Neutrality means that no one is accountable for interpretations

Blockchain data is public. It is not usable at institutional scale. Despite being open, blockchain data is fragmented, hard to interpret, and painful to maintain. Even a simple question like “Who are the largest Ethereum token holders over time?” can require running nodes, ingesting full chain history, decoding contracts, cleaning edge cases, and writing complex SQL.

Blockchains are optimized for writes, not reads.

They are built for consensus and execution, not searchability, standardization, or financial interpretation. Blockchains are computers, not databases. Every protocol defines its own schema. The same economic action can be encoded in dozens of different ways. The result:

  • Fragmented standards

  • Exponential complexity

  • No accountability for interpretation

  • Events without economic meaning

Finance cannot operate on that, it needs an effective system of record.

Allium is building the System of Record for Onchain Finance

Allium ingests, verifies, and standardizes data across 140+ blockchains and 30+ petabytes of history. We close four structural gaps that prevent blockchains from becoming systems of record:

  • Semantic Gap: Translating raw events into financial concepts like payments, trades, deposits, and staking income

  • Standardization Gap: Mapping thousands of protocols into a single canonical cross chain schema

  • Infrastructure Gap: Read optimized, globally distributed data at web scale

  • Accountability Gap: Auditable methodology, SLAs, and SOC 1 and 2 compliance

The result is a neutral, canonical data layer institutions can build on with confidence.

Finance is moving onchain

Stablecoins, tokenized assets, trading, staking, and lending are growing rapidly. Institutions need a trusted source of truth for onchain financial activity, just as they rely on Bloomberg or DTCC in traditional markets. Raw blockchains cannot serve that role.

As AI agents begin transacting autonomously, the requirement becomes even stricter. Agents cannot reason over raw event logs. They need structured data, attribution, condition checks, and auditability.

Allium is the read layer that makes onchain finance usable for humans and machines.

Who We Serve

Allium powers three core personas with the same canonical data foundation:

1. Finance, Accounting, and Risk Teams They need reliable, audit grade answers. They rely on Allium for financial reporting, reconciliation, compliance, risk monitoring, and defensible metrics that can stand up to auditors and regulators.

About the role

We're hiring a hands-on security leader to own Allium's security program and employee IT environment. You'll set priorities, implement controls, and partner with Engineering and business teams to protect the systems and data our company depends on.

AI is changing how software is built and how attackers operate. We want someone who can help Allium use agents and automation safely while building effective defenses against credential theft, compromised dependencies, and fast-moving attacks. You'll combine technical execution with ownership of a growing function, working directly on problems while shaping the team, tools, and specialist support we need.

What you'll do

  • Own the security roadmap. Assess our environment, prioritize material risks, and turn priorities into implemented controls with clear owners. Give leadership a concise view of progress, unresolved exposure, and decisions that require their judgment.

  • Set the security approach for AI agents. Establish practical standards for agent identities, tool permissions, credential handling, execution isolation, data access, and logging. Partner with Engineering to evaluate coding assistants, model gateways, and integrations, and test for prompt injection, tool misuse, and unintended actions.

  • Own employee IT and workforce security. Own the coverage and effectiveness of controls across employee devices, identities, cloud environments, and critical SaaS applications. Track exceptions, assign remediation owners, and build reliable onboarding and offboarding processes. Define how routine IT support is delivered through internal resources or providers.

  • Strengthen cloud and software security. Reduce standing privilege and strengthen separation between employee devices, development environments, and production. Establish practical standards for credential storage and privileged access. Partner with Engineering on secure development, CI/CD, and software supply-chain controls.

  • Lead detection, response, and recovery. Build a coordinated program across cloud, identity, development, employee systems, and agent activity. Define responsibilities for internal teams and providers, maintain escalation paths, and test containment, credential-revocation, and recovery procedures with system owners.

  • Build a fast, evidence-based vulnerability response. Maintain visibility into internet-facing services, including developer tools and management interfaces. Experience that would be helpful

Don't take our word for it, what our customers say about us (https://www.allium.so/blog#love)

Ok, now for some tough love. Here are the values we strive for at Allium:

  • Obsessiveness - The best people at Allium cannot put a problem down once they pick it up. We care more about the work than is strictly rational. Institutions trust us because our data is right. Right means caring about the small things. The decoded contract that ships with one wrong field. The label that is 99% accurate but wrong on the address that matters. The query that runs in 4 seconds when it should run in 400 milliseconds. Most companies tolerate these. We do not.

    Obsessiveness shows up as depth of care. It is not measured in hours worked or visible effort. You should feel something physical when work ships half-right. That instinct is what we hire for.

  • Pro Athlete Mindset - Consistency. Day in and day out, in pursuit of excellence. A win yesterday does not guarantee (or even imply!) a win tomorrow. I hope anyone who supports a failing sports team will feel the pain (cough Man United fans) of inconsistency

If you can’t learn it, find someone or a product that does it. If you can’t find someone, find someone who can find someone. It is never a lack of resources, but lack of resourcefulness.

  • High Agency - (One of) the highest commonalities between all successful people is their responsiveness. Most successful billionaire CEOs still reply to emails within minutes (within working hours). And when you reply, respond fast with effective solutions - and even better, resolutions. If you’re looking for a superpower, you can’t go wrong with responsiveness. Well of course this doesn't make sense when you're an engineer coding in flow, but in general high agency of problem solving gets one very far in life

We invite people of all backgrounds (https://www.allium.so/about).
